# Weights within a ratio agree past it

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`weights-within-a-ratio-agree-past-it` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F07 · [record](weights-within-a-ratio-agree-past-it.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Every positive weighting whose weights stand within n/d of each other ranks the course keeping p items the other does not above the one keeping q exactly where n q < d p; two such weightings rank a pair opposite ways exactly where n/d exceeds both p/q and q/p.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Where every two listed weights stand within n/d, what each course alone admits bounds what it weighs: d times what the second alone admits weighs, once per item the first alone admits, is at most n times the number the second alone admits, times what the first alone admits weighs. (`Becoming.Weighting.RatioWithin`, `Becoming.Weighting.cond_scale`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_scale`, `Becoming.Weighting.mul_swap_right`, `Becoming.Weighting.beyond_within`)
2. Every positive weighting within n/d ranks a above b where n q < d p, and weighs a at least as much where n q ≤ d p, p and q the numbers of items a and b alone admit. (`Becoming.Weighting.pos_of_lt_mul`, `Becoming.Weighting.cond_pos_of`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_pos_of_size`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_zero_of_size`, `Becoming.Weighting.ranks_past_ratio`, `Becoming.Weighting.ranks_le_past_ratio`)
3. The weighting tilted toward b, n on what b alone admits and d elsewhere, is positive and within n/d for 0 < d ≤ n; it ranks a above b exactly where n q < d p and ties them on the boundary n q = d p. (`Becoming.Weighting.tilted`, `Becoming.Weighting.cond_between`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilted_positive`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilted_within`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilt_beyond`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilt_toward`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_tilted_beyond`, `Becoming.Weighting.weighed_tilted_toward`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilted_lt_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilted_gt_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.tilted_ties`)
4. For 0 < d ≤ n: every positive weighting within n/d ranks a above b exactly where n q < d p; some ranks b above a exactly where d p < n q; two rank them opposite ways exactly where d q < n p and d p < n q. (`Becoming.Weighting.every_within_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.some_within_reverses_iff`, `Becoming.Weighting.opposite_within_iff`)
5. Equal weights are the ratio one: under one positive weight a course weighs more exactly where it admits more beyond the other than the other beyond it, so it ranks by number; the weighting tilted toward a course admitting an item the other does not, with weight one more than the listing's length, ranks it higher. (`Becoming.Weighting.const_lt_iff_beyond`, `Becoming.Weighting.size_le_length`, `Becoming.Weighting.size_pos_of_exceeds`, `Becoming.Weighting.outweighs`, `Becoming.Weighting.neutral_ranks_by_number`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. A finite listing of items; two-valued admission; natural weights positive on every listed item; the ratio n/d with 0 < d ≤ n for the exact forms (0 < n for the weak one); p and q counted with the listing's repetitions.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- How dispersed actual valuers' weights are, or that their valuations are additive: dispersion is a premise to measure.
- How many valuers disagree: the laws say which weightings can rank a pair opposite ways, not their share; no probability over weights is stated.
- The threshold for orders that are not additive: an order increasing in admission but not additive need not follow it.
- That the larger side is better: counting is a further premise, and C ranks neither side of a mixed pair.
- **Counterexample:** On the boundary n q = d p the tilted weighting ties the two courses (Weighting.tilted_ties), and short of it, d p < n q, it ranks the smaller side higher (Weighting.tilted_gt_iff): the threshold is exact. <details><summary>Correspondence, dependencies, sources and history</summary>

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Equal weights and improper linear models (Einhorn and Hogarth 1975; Dawes 1979; Wilks 1938): equal weights approximate estimated ones; here the exact ordinal form for two-valued courses. Dominance under partial information on weights (Kirkwood and Sarin 1985; imprecise ratio statements, Salo and Hämäläinen 1992): the tilted weighting is the extreme point that decides. Robust ordinal regression (Greco, Mousseau and Słowiński 2008): under the ratio bound the necessary relation is n q < d p and a possible reversal d p < n q. Reading (the AI's): "valuers count" (VD1) is weights mostly dispersed less than the pairs' ratios; VD1's mixed pairs kept 2 : 1, 3 : 1 and 1 : 1, so disagreement among valuers whose weights stand within twofold falls only on the last, where it was highest.
